gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 7?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 7 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Official observations from the German Weather Service will resolve the market once final readings are confirmed. Unexpected shifts such as increased cloud cover, localized showers, or revisions in the final model runs could still alter the measured maximum.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency project a maximum of 35°C for Tokyo on August 8 under partly cloudy skies, yet trader consensus clusters tightly around 33–34°C amid model spreads in sea-breeze timing and afternoon cloud development that can shave 1–2°C from peak readings. High humidity near 70–80% and the urban heat island effect amplify apparent temperatures, but variable wind patterns and any earlier marine layer intrusion often cap actual maxima below guidance. Historical August baselines average 30–32°C, so the narrow 33–34°C band reflects ongoing uncertainty in short-term convective inhibition and observational updates before the daily close.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 9 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/jp/tokyo/RJTT.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Japan Meteorological Agency forecasts project a mostly cloudy day with a high near 35°C for Tokyo on August 9, driven by the persistent Pacific High advecting warm, moist air masses northward. Trader consensus clusters tightly around 32–33°C because models show potential for increased cloud cover and scattered showers that could limit peak solar heating by 1–3°C compared to clearer analogs. Differentiation among these outcomes hinges on precise timing of any frontal passages or convective development, which alter surface energy budgets and boundary-layer mixing; historical August variability in the Kanto region often produces 2–4°C swings from such factors, keeping near-term model runs and observational updates as key market movers.
